summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Portuguese golden-visa (ARI) documents: three AIMA annual migration reports, the AIMA fee table and ARI web page, the 2014 IGAI audit of SEF's ARI procedure, and 14 laws and regulations. Most were already fully reflected in the data; new rows come from the IGAI audit (file counts by SEF office, ARI fee revenue by office, remaining 2014 fees, the 2013 order cutting the job route to 10), the 2026 fee table (family, copy, replacement and permanent-residence fees), the web page (low-density reduced minimums) and one event for Decreto Regulamentar 1/2024.

program_terms.notes: Joint ministerial order (despacho) 1661-A/2013 of 28 Jan 2013 cut the job-creation route from 30 to 10 jobs; IGAI argues an order cannot override the 30 jobs in Law 29/2012 (p. 93). Law 63/2015 later wrote 10 jobs into the law.

events.title: Regulation adapts golden-visa rules to Mais Habitação and AIMA
events.description: Decreto Regulamentar 1/2024 (published 17 Jan 2024, in force the next day) amends the 2007 immigration regulation: AIMA's board decides ARI applications; the 20% low-density reduction applies only to job creation, research and culture; proof of investment is checked in agency databases (AICEP, Banco Português de Fomento, ANI, GEPAC, social security); permanent ARI for holders and families is not lost through absences; renewals of real-estate and capital-transfer ARIs follow the entrepreneur-immigrant rules; ARI fees are those of Portaria 307/2023.
events.quote: Os investimentos previstos nas subalíneas ii), v) e vi) da alínea d) do n.º 1 do artigo 3.º

events.title: Ministerial order lowers job-creation route to 10 jobs and sets minimum stay
events.description: Joint order (Despacho) 1661-A/2013 of the Foreign and Interior Ministers amended Despacho 11820-A/2012: the job-creation route was cut from 30 to 10 jobs and the minimum stay set at 7 days in the first year and 14 days in later periods. IGAI later called the job change unlawful because an order cannot amend the law.
events.quote: o despacho n.º 1661-A/2013 alterou a redação da alínea b), do n.º 1, do artigo 3.º do despacho n.º 11.820-A/2012

gaps: AIMA reports for 2023-2025 publish only annual ARI totals, family permits and top nationalities: no routes, investment amounts, applications or monthly figures (unlike the SEF monthly maps, which end in Sep 2023).

IGAI audit (2014) gives several approximate operational figures (about 90% of applications at DRLVTA, about 300 approved files awaiting fee payment, up to 100 ARI appointments a day) with no fitting indicator; left as a to-do.

ledger.contains: AIMA annual migration and asylum report 2023 (43 pp.): general residence-permit statistics (new permits by reason, age, district, CPLP, nationality annex, stock of foreign residents 1980-2023), contact centre, returns, asylum. ARI content is one page (PDF p. 15, printed p. 11): 2 901 ARI permits granted in 2023, 1 554 family-reunification permits, and a labelled chart of the five main nationalities (USA 567, China 306, UK 234, Brazil 219, India 199). All of these were already in the data; whole report also OCR-checked for other investment mentions (none). Everything else is general immigration, out of scope.

AIMA annual migration and asylum report 2024 (42 pp.): general residence-permit statistics, contact centre, returns, asylum, nationality annex, glossary (defines "atividade de investimento" with current thresholds). ARI content is one page (PDF p. 18, printed p. 14): 2 081 ARI permits in 2024, 2 909 family-reunification permits, and an image bar chart of eight main nationalities (USA 406, China 296, Russia 248, UK 147, India 140, Turkey 128, South Africa 100, Brazil 98). All already in the data; OCR of all pages found no other ARI figures, no routes or investment amounts.

AIMA annual migration and asylum report 2025 (71 pp.): general residence-permit statistics, service figures, returns, asylum, glossary. ARI content is one page (PDF p. 21, printed p. 17): 2 685 ARI permits in 2025, 3 967 family-reunification permits, and an image bar chart of eight main nationalities (USA 535, China 392, UK 252, Turkey 188, India 170, Russia 160, Brazil 154, South Africa 97). All already in the data; OCR of all pages found no other ARI figures, no routes or investment amounts.

AIMA web page "Autorização de Residência para Investimento – Art. 90.º-A" (retrieved 2 Oct 2026): regime in force since 8 Oct 2012; benefits (minimum stay 7 days in the first year, 14 days in later years; family reunification; permanent residence; naturalisation); the five current routes with minimums (10 jobs; EUR 500k research; EUR 250k culture; EUR 500k non-real-estate funds; EUR 500k company with 5/10 jobs) and document lists; family members eligible; permit valid two years; legislation list. No statistics. Standard minimums are already in the data from the laws; added the low-density reduced amounts the page prints (8 jobs, EUR 400k research, EUR 220k culture, the last inconsistent with its own 20% rule). The 2012 launch event already cites this page.

Decreto-Lei 14/2021 (4 pp.): amends arts. 3 and 90-A of Law 23/2007 under the 2020 budget authorisation: capital transfer EUR 1.5m; research, fund and company routes EUR 500k; residential real estate (subalíneas iii and iv) only in the Azores, Madeira and interior territories (Portaria 208/2017); applies to applications after entry into force; renewals and family permits of existing holders unaffected; in force 1 Jan 2022. All amounts and both dates already in the data (6 terms, 2 events). No statistics.

Law 63/2015 (2 pp.), third amendment to Law 23/2007: art. 3(1)(d) adds subalíneas iv-vii (EUR 350k rehabilitation, EUR 350k research, EUR 250k culture, EUR 500k SME funds) and cuts job creation to 10; art. 3(2)-(3) allow 20% lower amounts for ii-vi in low-density NUTS III areas; decision deadlines for all permits (90/60 days, general, not ARI-specific); adult student children as ARI family members; repeals art. 90-A(3) (regulation by ministerial order); in force the day after 30 Jun 2015. All ARI amounts already in the data (5 terms, low-density rule in their notes) and the event. Also prints, on its second page, an unrelated parliamentary resolution on financial stability. No statistics.

Portaria 208/2017 (4 pp., with unrelated notices on the same DR pages): defines the "interior territories" (165 municipalities and 73 parishes listed by NUTS III) for the National Territorial Cohesion Programme, used by DL 14/2021 to limit residential golden-visa purchases from 2022 and for the 20% low-density reduction. Only a list of places; no numbers about the programme. Its role is described in the notes of the real-estate terms.

Law 61/2025 (9 pp.) amending Law 23/2007: new qualified job-seeker visa, CPLP permits, family reunification only after two years of residence (15 months for some spouses) with exemptions, integration measures, nine-month decision deadline for reunification, court remedies against AIMA, deadline for expression-of-interest cases, bilateral labour agreements. The only ARI provision (family members of art. 90-A holders exempt from the two-year wait, art. 98(3)(c)) is already an event. Other content is general immigration, out of scope. No statistics.

Organic Law 2/2006 (7 pp.), fourth amendment to the Nationality Law with republication: naturalisation after six years of legal residence (art. 6(1)(b)), definition of legal residence, other nationality rules. The six-year rule that applied to golden-visa holders from 2012 to 2018 is recorded in the programme description (programs.csv cites this law); it predates the programme, so no event is added. No statistics or amounts.

Organic Law 2/2018 (8 pp.), eighth amendment to the Nationality Law with republication: naturalisation after five years of legal residence (was six), wider birthright rules. The five-year change is already an event; the rest is not specific to the programme. No statistics or amounts.

Organic Law 1/2024 (18 pp.), tenth amendment to the Nationality Law with republication: legal residence for naturalisation counted from the date the residence permit was applied for (if granted), other rules on descendants of Sephardic Jews, adoption, etc.; in force on the first day of the month after publication. The relevant change is already an event. No statistics or amounts.

Organic Law 1/2026 (19 pp.) amending the Nationality Law with republication: naturalisation after 7 years of legal residence for CPLP/EU nationals and 10 years for others, language/culture test, revokes counting from the permit application date, pending procedures stay under the old law, in force the day after 18 May 2026. Already an event; no statistics or amounts.

Decreto-Lei 41/2023 (87 pp.) creating AIMA and abolishing SEF (in force 29 Oct 2023): AIMA organic statute, transfer of SEF functions to AIMA, PSP, GNR, PJ and IRN, amendments to Law 23/2007 (fees go to AIMA, art. 209; SEF fee revenue becomes AIMA's, art. 46), staff transitions. No ARI-specific provision beyond the change of authority, which is already an event. No statistics or amounts about the programme.

Decreto Regulamentar 15-A/2015 (37 pp.), amending Decreto Regulamentar 84/2007 with full republication: new arts. 65-A to 65-J regulating ARI (minimum amounts per route restating Law 63/2015; co-ownership with each owner investing the minimum; mortgages only above the minimum; promissory contract with a deposit of at least the minimum; 20% low-density reduction; five-year period counted from the grant; minimum stay 7 days in the first year and 14 days in each later two-year period; proof documents for grant and renewal; investor information desks; monitoring group meeting monthly; procedures manual); in force the day after 2 Sep 2015. Amounts are already terms (from the laws, with these conditions in their notes) and the stay rule is an event. The rest of the republication is general immigration regulation. No statistics.

Law 102/2017 (74 pp.), fifth amendment to Law 23/2007 with full republication: fund route lowered to EUR 350k (Portuguese funds, 5-year maturity, 60% in Portuguese companies) and new company-capital route (EUR 350k with 5 jobs); ARI renewed for two-year periods (art. 90-A(2)); other changes on students, researchers, entrepreneurs, Blue Card. Both ARI amounts are already terms and the change is an event; the rest of the republication restates earlier ARI amounts or concerns other permits. No statistics.

Law 29/2012 (66 pp.), first amendment to Law 23/2007 with full republication: defines "atividade de investimento" (EUR 1m capital transfer, 30 jobs, EUR 500k real estate, for five years), adds art. 90-A (ARI without residence visa, Schengen visa, regularise within 90 days, renewals for two years, conditions set by ministerial order), plus Blue Card and other immigration changes; in force 60 days after 9 Aug 2012. The three amounts are terms and creation is an event; everything else is general immigration. No statistics.

Law 56/2023 (Mais Habitação), consolidated version of 29 Dec 2023 (49 pp.): housing, rental and tax measures, and Chapter V on ARI (arts. 42-44): no new ARI applications under capital transfer and real estate (subalíneas i, iii, iv) from entry into force; renewals and family permits continue but convert into entrepreneur-immigrant permits with the 7/14-day stay; pending applications kept; fund route EUR 500k limited to non-real-estate funds; company route EUR 500k with 5 new or 10 kept jobs; 20% low-density reduction now only for ii, v and vi; biennial impact evaluation; no real-estate investment for remaining routes. All already in the data (2 terms, 2 events, reduction rule in term notes). Housing and tax measures are out of scope. No statistics.

Decreto Regulamentar 1/2024 (45 pp.) amending Decreto Regulamentar 84/2007 after the creation of AIMA and Law 56/2023: general immigration procedures moved to AIMA, database-based proof (new art. 42-R lists minimum amounts per ARI route: 10 jobs, EUR 500k company with 5/10 jobs, EUR 500k non-real-estate funds, EUR 500k research, EUR 250k culture, restating the law), ARI articles 65-A to 65-K amended (low-density 20% only for ii, v, vi; AIMA board decides; monitoring group; biennial evaluation; procedures manual; permanent ARI), transitional rules for renewals of closed routes and fee payment deadlines (10 and 15 working days). Added one event (in force 18 Jan 2024). Amounts restate existing terms. No statistics.

AIMA fee table for procedures under Law 23/2007 (Portaria 307/2023, updated 26 Feb 2026), 8 pp., standard and reduced (digital/assisted) columns: stay extensions, temporary and permanent permits, Blue Card, long-term residents, travel documents, forms, urgent service, Brexit cards, EU citizens' certificates and certified copies. In scope is point III.3 (ARI): processing EUR 842.80, ARI issue EUR 8,418.90, renewal EUR 4,210.30 (already in the data) and, added now, family-reunification permit and renewal, second/third card copies, card replacement, and permanent residence for ARI holders (grant EUR 11,786.70, renewal EUR 5,894.10), each with its reduced amount in notes; point III.4 (ARI fee revenue split 50/50 between AIMA and the Foreign Ministry's FRI) noted. All other sections are general immigration fees, out of scope.

IGAI extraordinary audit of SEF's ARI (golden visa) procedure, 106 pp., dated 30 Dec 2014: legal framework (Law 29/2012, Despachos 11820-A/2012 and 1661-A/2013), visits to 13 SEF units with counts of ARI and family-reunification files per office, procedural findings, internal control, ARI fee schedule (p. 99) and ARI fee revenue by SEF unit since 1 Jan 2014 (p. 100), 20 conclusions and 18 recommendations. Extracted now: file counts (DRLVTA 4 365; other 11 units 422 = 190 ARI + 232 family; per-office counts for Portalegre, Portimão, Algarve, Madeira, Aveiro, Leiria, Cascais), 20 jobs created by two Aveiro investors, ARI fee revenue per unit in both ARI columns, the remaining ARI fees (family permits, card copies, replacement), and the 2013 order lowering the job route to 10 jobs. Already in data: ~2 000 pending files, total ARI fees 21,2m, issue/renewal/processing fees, audit event. Not ARI-specific and left out: the per-unit "Total" fee column (all SEF fees) and "Valor pago CGD" column. Table check: p. 100 columns add up to printed totals; Madeira count prints 11 + 21 = "33" (sum is 32).
